lines: Avery Brooks
+1 (555) 010-3319 | avery.brooks@example.com | example.com/in/abrooks
Date of birth: 9 Jan 1998 | Nationality: Brazilian
EDUCATION
Eastmoor University | B.S. in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Pinecrest Insurance | Junior Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Jul 2022
- Owned the claims backlog report and the weekly numbers the claims managers used.
- Analyzed 18 months of call-center data; my findings moved two agents to the evening peak and cut average hold time from 9 to 5 minutes.
- Wrote the team's SQL style guide and review checklist, which cut query errors found in review by half.

- Automated the monthly fraud-flag extract while also maintaining the team calendar, answering ad hoc questions from sales, updating onboarding documents and covering the help desk on Fridays, which saved the fraud team 10 hours a month.
Brightcart Retail | Data Analyst | Metro City, USA | Aug 2022 - Jun 2025
- Improved reporting efficiency by 90% by moving the monthly revenue report to scheduled SQL queries.
- Found customers with no orders by left-joining the orders table to the customers table and counting rows with a null customer name.
- Wrote data-quality checks on the 40 most-used tables, catching 15 broken loads before they reached a dashboard.
- Presented the quarterly customer review to the leadership team, and two of its three recommendations were funded in the next budget.
- Reported the national conversion rate as the simple average of 14 regional conversion rates, without weighting by regional traffic.
- Built the weekly retention dashboard for 2.4M customers that marketing used to retarget lapsed buyers, lifting 90-day repeat purchase from 22% to 27%.
PROJECTS
City Bike-Share Demand Study | Independent Project | Python, SQL | Jan 2025 - Present
- Modeled hourly bike-share demand for 120 stations from 2 years of public trip data, forecasting next-day demand within 12% mean absolute error.
- Compared the forecast with the operator's rebalancing schedule: empty-station hours fell from 310 to 205 a week in a replay of last summer.
- Published the notebooks and a short write-up, which the city's open-data team linked from its bike-share page.
Food Pantry Visit Analysis | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Excel, SQL | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Mapped 14 months of pantry visits by hour and day, so the pantry moved one volunteer shift and cut the Saturday line from 50 to 20 minutes.
- Cleaned 9,000 handwritten visit logs into a single table and matched repeat visitors, giving the pantry its first count of unique households.
- Built a retention dashboard for about 2.4 million shoppers that raised repeat purchases by nearly a quarter.
SKILLS
Tools: SQL, Python, Excel
Methods: dashboards, forecasting, metric design, data-quality checks

items.says: Remove the date of birth.
items.because: It is not needed for a typical U.S. resume and can invite irrelevant bias.

items.says: Remove or reconsider nationality.
items.because: Nationality itself usually is not relevant; include work-authorization information only when relevant.

items.says: The join direction is wrong for finding customers with no orders.
items.because: Starting from orders can exclude customers who have no matching order.

items.says: A null customer name is not a reliable test for an unmatched order.
items.because: It would not reliably identify customers without orders.

items.says: The claim about 2.4 million shoppers and retail purchases does not fit the pantry project.
items.because: The scale and retail context are inconsistent with the project.

items.says: The dashboard claim duplicates the Brightcart result.
items.because: It will undermine trust in the rest of the resume.

items.says: The unweighted national conversion rate is a flawed calculation presented as an accomplishment.
items.because: It may raise questions about analytical judgment.

items.says: Put Brightcart before Pinecrest.
items.because: Experience should be in reverse chronological order.

items.says: Check that the profile URL works and its displayed link is recognizable and professional.
items.because: Contact information should be easy to scan.

items.says: Consider placing Experience before Education.
items.because: You have several years of experience.

items.says: Specify the scope of your responsibility and what “the weekly numbers” means.
items.because: The scope is vague.

items.says: Explain why the claims backlog report mattered, ideally with a measure of its scale or use.
items.because: The result is vague.

items.says: Clarify whether your analysis led to the staffing change or contributed to a broader decision.
items.because: Your role in the hold-time reduction is unclear.

items.says: Add a relevant timeframe or data volume.
items.because: It would help establish scale.

items.says: Clarify the period and basis for the reduction “by half,” including error or query counts if known.
items.because: That would make the result measurable and credible.

items.says: Prioritize the fraud-extract automation over the unrelated duties.
items.because: Combining them obscures the impact.

items.says: Quantify what the 10 monthly hours represent.
Define “reporting efficiency” in practical terms.
items.because: “Efficiency” is not defined.

items.says: Give the 90% improvement a defensible baseline.
Add the period over which the checks caught 15 broken loads, if available.
items.because: It would help readers judge the scale.

items.says: Clarify your own contribution to the quarterly review.
Explain what the funded recommendations addressed, if possible.
items.because: “Two of three were funded” alone does not show their significance.

items.says: Clarify the measurement period, cohort definition, and how the repeat-purchase lift was assessed.
Clarify whether the dashboard or related work can reasonably be credited with the lift.
items.because: The result is phrased causally.

items.says: Distinguish a percentage-point change from a percentage change.
Clarify what “within 12% mean absolute error” measures.
items.because: MAE is usually expressed in forecast units, while a percentage suggests a normalized or relative measure.

items.says: Explain how the forecast was validated.
items.because: That would help readers assess it.

items.says: Make explicit that the reduction came from a replay or simulation.
items.because: It should not be mistaken for a measured real-world reduction.

items.says: Explain the replay’s comparison period or assumptions.
Ensure the notebooks and write-up are accessible and the city’s link is still live.
Keep “Present” only if the project is still active.
Make clear the overlapping dates reflect a side project.
items.because: The overlap with Brightcart could imply a gap or a conflicting job.

items.says: Clarify your role in the volunteer-shift recommendation or evaluation.
Explain how the Saturday line-time change was measured.
Explain the practical use or outcome of the unique-household count, if there was one.
Be prepared to explain how you handled ambiguous handwritten records and repeat-visitor matching.
Consider adding other tools or platforms you have used.
items.because: The list may be too limited for the roles you want.

items.says: Tailor and substantiate the broad methods listed.
items.because: “Dashboards,” “forecasting,” and “data-quality checks” are broad.

items.says: Be prepared to explain “metric design.”
items.because: The conversion-rate issue makes it especially worth substantiating.

items.says: Keep dates, locations, punctuation, and bullet formatting consistent throughout.
items.because: The resume should be easy to scan.
